What is the difference between input() in Python 2 and Python 3?

Supplied answer
In Python 3, input() always returns a string, so conversion is needed. In Python 2, raw_input() returned a
string while input() evaluated whatever was typed - which was unsafe. Other Python 3 differences: print
is a function, integer division uses //, and strings are Unicode by default.
